statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 14 is in the low band and well below the block threshold.
recommendation: The 29,660 shelf that rejected three times has been cleared and NQ holds within ten points of a new session high, which lifts the assessment, while decaying volatility and an unchanged 10-year keep it in the low band. The mapped policy state is EA_ON. The single mapped danger window is 14:00-15:30 UTC on Aug 28 around the Jackson Hole keynote and the final Michigan sentiment reading. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged.
headline: NQ clears the thrice-rejected 29,660 shelf to a new session high at 29,675.75, but VIX sets a fresh 14.42 low and the 10-year is unchanged; Tail edges to 14
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 29,666.25, up 376.75 points or 1.29% from the 29,289.50 prior settlement, roughly four hours into the U.S. cash session. The session range is 29,401.75-29,675.75 against a 29,499.50 open. The decisive change since the prior assessment is that the 29,660 area, which rejected three separate times earlier in the session, has now been cleared: the market printed a new session high at 29,675.75 and holds within ten points of it. That is observed session-extreme holding and it is the reason the assessment steps up rather than down. Cash confirms the move. QQQ trades at 719.74, up 1.18%, having extended its range high to 720.62 from 719.58 an hour earlier, against an unchanged 714.53 session low. The advance is broad within technology and narrow outside it: reported index moves put the Nasdaq composite up roughly 1.4-1.5% and the S&P 500 up 0.7-0.8%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average adds only about 0.3-0.4%. Nvidia trades up about 9% on its Q2 beat and above-consensus Q3 revenue guidance, Salesforce up about 21%, CrowdStrike about 18% and Okta about 22%, with the expanded technology-software ETF up about 6%. This is a sector-concentrated repricing of AI demand rather than a whole-market directional regime. The counterweights are substantial and they are what keep Tail in the low band. Volatility is decaying through the advance rather than expanding with it: VIX trades at 14.50, down 4.67% from a 15.21 prior close, and has set a fresh session low at 14.42 inside a 14.42-15.13 range. Rates are inert: the 10-year yield reads 4.664%, unchanged on the session inside a narrow 4.649-4.672 band, with the H.15 release showing 4.64% on the 10-year and 4.17% on the 2-year at the most recent observation. An index up 1.3% whose volatility index makes new lows and whose long-end yield does not move is not a stress repricing, and the absence of cross-asset alignment removes the main amplifier that would otherwise accompany a breakout. Energy is quiet and two-sided: WTI trades near 82.70 dollars, up 0.57%, and Brent near 88.74 dollars, up 1.02%, with improving Strait of Hormuz supply prospects weighed against disruption to Russian exports. Today's U.S. data was mildly supportive and is fully absorbed: initial jobless claims printed 203,000 against 208,000 expected and continuing claims 1.778 million against 1.790 million, while the advance goods trade balance came in materially wider at -118.8 billion dollars against -99 billion expected without producing a visible index reaction. Most importantly for a mean-reversion assessment, this session has already demonstrated that retracements deliver: the prior hour produced a marginal new high, a rejection, and roughly 130 points handed back before the level finally gave way on the fourth attempt. A range that was defended three times and then broke is a genuine amplifier and Tail rises to 14 to reflect it, but a single shallow breakout of about fifteen points above a defended shelf, inside a total daily range under 1%, with volatility falling and rates unchanged, is not the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures. The dominant catalyst is resolved rather than pending, which removes the delayed second-leg mechanism that normally justifies broader protection. Confidence is 87: futures, cash proxy, volatility, rates, energy and the verified macro calendar are all current within the last twenty minutes, with a modest deduction because the shared cross-asset context file is roughly four hours old and therefore outside its freshness window, leaving breadth and megacap detail sourced from reporting rather than from a structured feed.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours cover the Nvidia release and its complete digestion into a broad technology advance. From 17:00 UTC on Aug 26 the regime was mixed and calm at Tail 10-11 while Stress climbed to 61 as positioning built into the report. The 20:00 UTC release hour was the only non-green hour in the window, moving to WATCH at Tail 21 and Stress 66. Futures reopened at 22:00 UTC on the beat and raised guidance, and the assessment stepped down through 18, 16, 13 and 12 in event/whipsaw mode as the gap held without extending. From 03:00 UTC the regime returned to mixed at Tail 10-11 with Stress easing to 45-47 through the Asian and European hours, the calmest stretch of the window. The 13:00 UTC hour lifted to Tail 14 and Stress 54 into the cash open, then eased back through 12, 12 and 11 as the opening auction faded and the range absorbed flow rather than extending. Three hours are unavailable because no assessment was published for them: 21:00 UTC on Aug 26 during the futures maintenance break, and 00:00 and 09:00 UTC on Aug 27. Every available hour except the release hour mapped to EA_ON.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours contain a quiet U.S. afternoon, an empty overnight and one genuine catalyst cluster at the far edge. With the 29,660 shelf now cleared, conditional Tail holds at 14 through the rest of today's cash session and lifts to 15 across the 19:00 UTC closing hour for closing imbalances and month-end positioning. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the estimate steps down, with the 21:00 UTC maintenance break the structural low of the horizon at 9, and holds a 10-11 overnight floor through the Asian hours in normal mode. From the 07:00 UTC European open the path drifts up through 11-13 as the keynote countdown compresses positioning, reaching 14 in the U.S. pre-market and 16 in the 13:00 UTC hour that carries the Friday cash open alongside Chicago PMI. The only two hours outside the low band are the last of the horizon: conditional Tail 22 at 14:00 UTC, where the Fed chair's Jackson Hole keynote and the final Michigan sentiment reading land in the same minute, and 20 at 15:00 UTC for the structurally multi-stage second leg that can follow central-bank communication. Event weight is carried mainly by Stress, which climbs from 49 to 71 across the horizon, rather than by an asserted price path: nothing about the keynote's content can be known at the assessment cutoff.
